The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by James Hunt | Edited by Jason Shubnell

Presented By:

( https://bron.org/?utm_source=TheBlock&utm_medium=Email&utm_campaign=DailyNewsletter&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Happy Wednesday! *Bitcoin* is still hovering below $80,000 ahead of Friday's *CPI* print, with *Bitget* analyst *Lewis Huang* telling The Block the cryptocurrency has shown "unusually high sensitivity" to shifting U.S. rate expectations over the past week, while *LMAX Group* Market Strategist *Joel Kruger* said the recent corrective phase may be nearing its end.

In today's newsletter, *Jack Dorsey's Block* seeks to become a federally regulated national bank, *MetaMask* splits from *Consensys* , *Tether* and *Fasanara* launch a $400 million private credit fund, and more.

Meanwhile, the *Ink Foundation* , *GSR* , and several law and audit firms opened the *Charter Foundation* ( https://www.theblock.co/news/ecosystems/2026-09-09-ink-foundation-gsr-crypto-charter-foundation-token-launch-costs-414023?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) to help crypto founders cut token launch costs.

*P.S.* Don't forget to check out The Funding , a biweekly rundown of crypto VC trends. It's a great read — and just like The Daily, it's free to subscribe ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?select=The+Funding&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) !

*THE BIG ONE*

*🏦 Jack Dorsey's Block joins rush for federal bank charters from OCC*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-09-08-jack-dorsey-block-joins-rush-federal-bank-charters-from-occ-413947?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Jack Dorsey's Block* filed with the *OCC* to establish an uninsured national trust bank called *Builders Bank & Trust* , joining the rush of crypto and fintech firms seeking federal charters.

* If approved, Builders Bank would offer custody and fiduciary services, including for *bitcoin* and stablecoins, giving Block a federal framework for activities it currently offers.
* *Lee Woolley* , set to run Builders Bank as president and CEO, pointed to Block's digital asset and *Square Financial Services* experience as the foundation for the new venture.
* The application comes after *Revolut's* conditional approval last week and follows a wave of others, including *Coinbase* , *Ripple* , *Circle* , *Paxos* , and *BitGo* , as the OCC takes a friendlier stance toward crypto.
* The OCC also recently granted conditional approval to *Trump*

78822.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works

Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/chatgpt-solved-1-million-math-problem-genai-works-1sirf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bmk7Cw3zxQxCsaW5Jw6OVeg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2v9eVDlAVcZso1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mtu999sz~z4-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mtu999sz-z4
  
Welcome back! OpenAI's agents cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, Anthropic's alignment lead put a percentage on human extinction, and Meta shipped an agent with a bodyguard.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: ChatGPT solved a $1 million math problem: Why is OpenAI refusing to take the prize money? Anthropic's science lead says we could all be dead in 10 years: What number did he put on it, and what did he say Anthropic doesn't have? Meta built a second agent to watch the first one: What does Sentinel stop Muse from doing? ChatGPT images got a whole lot better: Which upgrade finally fixes the thing every image model gets wrong? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. ChatGPT claims a Millennium Prize problem  One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, open for roughly 90 years, each carrying a $1 million prize. Second one ever resolved. The equations describe how fluids move and they sit underneath weather forecasting, aircraft design and blood flow models.  The open question was whether a fluid that starts out smooth can break down and produce infinite speed in finite time. The answer is yes.  The proof builds a vortex that spirals inward and stretches like spaghetti, shrinking and accelerating while its energy stays finite. Roughly 10,000 agents worked in parallel for 88 hours. Lean formalization and verification took another 17 hours, done by GPT-6 Astra. On this problem alone the agents sent 2.7 million messages and produced about 130 billion output tokens. Across all the problems they tried, 4.9 million messages and 300 billion tokens. The model behind it is internal and has only been training since August 28. Training is still running. OpenAI says it is significantly more capable than Astra, which shipped six days ago and had people calling it AGI. The agents also disproved regularity for the unforced Euler equations along the way, which took about 100 agents and 50 hours. Then the credit fight started.  Tristan Buckmaster at NYU and Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published hours earlier, and Buckmaster says OpenAI heard about their method and used it.  OpenAI says it launched the effort on September 1 after hearing a rumor it later connected to them, saw none of their work before publication, and offered them a joint announcement on September 6 along
